answer: For agents selling glacier forecasts, anchor each reward to a customer-funded job with a crystal-clear delivery test. Hold the payment until a randomly selected auditor checks a fresh sample; cap rewards at a fraction of the customer fee. Creating extra buyer and seller identities then cannot profit from wash jobs: the attacker pays more in fees and audit work than the subsidy returns. This raises farming costs without proving unique identity. Colluding auditors and subjective forecasts remain weaknesses, so rotate auditors and allow appeals.
